questions.questionText: In what ratio must tea at Rs. 62 per kg be mixed with tea at Rs. 72 per kg so that the mixture must be worth Rs. 64.50 per kg?
A vessel contains 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres of milk is taken out and replaced by water. This process is repeated two more times. How much milk is now left in the vessel?
questions.explanation: Formula: Remaining pure liquid = Initial * (1 - x / V)^n. Remaining milk = 80 * (1 - 8/80)^3 = 80 * (0.9)^3 = 80 * 0.729 = 58.32 litres.

questions.questionText: A merchant has 1000 kg of sugar, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. What is the quantity sold at 18% profit?
How many kg of rice at Rs. 54 per kg should be mixed with 30 kg of rice at Rs. 40 per kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 57.60 per kg there is a gain of 20%?
questions.explanation: Mean CP = 57.60 / 1.20 = Rs. 48 per kg. Alligation between Rs. 54 and Rs. 40 to get Rs. 48: Ratio = (48 - 40) : (54 - 48) = 8 : 6 = 4 : 3. For 3 parts = 30 kg, 4 parts = 40 kg.

questions.questionText: Two vessels A and B contain milk and water in the ratios 7 : 5 and 17 : 7 respectively. In what ratio should the mixtures from A and B be mixed to get a new mixture containing milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.explanation: Milk fraction in A = 7/12. Milk fraction in B = 17/24. Target milk fraction = 3/5. By Alligation: (17/24 - 3/5) : (3/5 - 7/12) = (85 - 72)/120 : (36 - 35)/60 = (13/120) : (2/120) = 13 : 2.

questions.questionText: A jar contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 4 : 1. When 10 litres of the mixture is taken out and 10 litres of liquid B is poured in, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. How many litres of liquid A was contained in the jar initially?
questions.explanation: Let initial quantities be 4x and x. When 10 L is removed: A removed = 8 L, B removed = 2 L. (4x - 8) / (x - 2 + 10) = 2/3 => (4x - 8)/(x + 8) = 2/3 => 3(4x - 8) = 2(x + 8) => 12x - 24 = 2x + 16 => 10x = 40 => x = 4. Initial liquid A = 4 * 4 = 16 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio should water be mixed with milk costing Rs. 12 per litre so as to make a profit of 20% by selling the mixture at cost price?
questions.explanation: When sold at CP, Profit% = (Water / Milk) * 100% = 20% => Water / Milk = 20 / 100 = 1 / 5.

questions.questionText: A can contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 7 : 5. When 9 litres of mixture are drawn off and the can is filled with B, the ratio of A and B becomes 7 : 9. How many litres of liquid A was contained by the can initially?
The cost of Type 1 rice is Rs. 15 per kg and Type 2 rice is Rs. 20 per kg. If both are mixed in the ratio 2 : 3, then the price per kg of the mixed variety of rice is:
In a 729 litre mixture of milk and water, the ratio of milk to water is 7 : 2. How much water should be added to get a new mixture containing milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 9. 1 part = 729 / 9 = 81 litres. Initial milk = 7 * 81 = 567 L, Water = 2 * 81 = 162 L. In new ratio 7 : 3, milk remains 567 L (7 parts => 1 part = 81 L). Required water = 3 * 81 = 243 L. Water to add = 243 - 162 = 81 litres.
questions.concept: Adding Water to Fixed Milk Baseline

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a grocer mix two varieties of pulses costing Rs. 15 and Rs. 20 per kg respectively so as to get a mixture worth Rs. 16.50 per kg?
A 20-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much milk should be added to make the ratio 4 : 1?
questions.explanation: Initial: Milk = 15 L, Water = 5 L. To make ratio 4 : 1 with 5 L water, total milk required = 4 * 5 = 20 L. Milk to add = 20 - 15 = 5 litres.
questions.concept: Milk Addition to Fixed Water Baseline

questions.questionText: A container contains 40 litres of milk. From this container, 4 litres of milk was taken out and replaced by water. This process was repeated further two times. How much milk is now contained by the container?
Two alloys A and B contain zinc and tin in the ratios 5 : 2 and 3 : 4 respectively. If 7 kg of alloy A and 21 kg of alloy B are mixed together, find the ratio of zinc to tin in the new alloy.
questions.explanation: Alloy A (7 kg): Zinc = 5 kg, Tin = 2 kg. Alloy B (21 kg, ratio 3:4, total 7 parts => 1 part = 3 kg): Zinc = 3 * 3 = 9 kg, Tin = 4 * 3 = 12 kg. Total Zinc = 5 + 9 = 14 kg. Total Tin = 2 + 12 = 14 kg. Ratio = 14 : 14 = 1 : 1.

questions.questionText: How many kg of sugar costing Rs. 9 per kg must be mixed with 27 kg of sugar costing Rs. 7 per kg so that there may be a gain of 10% by selling the mixture at Rs. 9.24 per kg?
questions.explanation: Mean CP = 9.24 / 1.10 = Rs. 8.40 per kg. Alligation between Rs. 9 and Rs. 7 to get Rs. 8.40: Ratio = (8.40 - 7) : (9 - 8.40) = 1.40 : 0.60 = 7 : 3. 3 parts = 27 kg => 1 part = 9 kg. 7 parts = 7 * 9 = 63 kg.

questions.questionText: A vessel of 60 litres is full of milk. 12 litres of milk is taken out and replaced by water. Again 12 litres of mixture is taken out and replaced by water. Find the ratio of milk and water in the final mixture.
In what ratio must a 30% alcohol solution be mixed with a 50% alcohol solution to get a 35% alcohol solution?
A mixture of 40 litres of milk and water contains 10% water. How much water should be added to this so that water may be 20% in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk in initial mixture = 90% of 40 = 36 litres. In new mixture, milk is 80%. Let total new mixture be T. 80% of T = 36 => T = 36 / 0.80 = 45 litres. Water to add = 45 - 40 = 5 litres.

questions.questionText: Two containers have milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1 and 5 : 3. If equal quantities are taken from both and mixed, find the ratio of milk to water in the resulting mixture.
questions.explanation: Container 1 (total 4 parts, scale by 2): Milk = 6/8, Water = 2/8. Container 2 (total 8 parts): Milk = 5/8, Water = 3/8. Total Milk = 6 + 5 = 11. Total Water = 2 + 3 = 5. Resulting ratio = 11 : 5.

questions.questionText: A butler steals wine from a butt of sherry containing 40% spirit and replaces what he stole with wine containing 16% spirit. The butt is then of 24% strength. How much of the butt did he steal?
questions.explanation: By Alligation: Original (40%) and Stolen Replacement (16%) mix to (24%). Ratio of original remaining to replaced = (24 - 16) : (40 - 24) = 8 : 16 = 1 : 2. Total butt = 1 + 2 = 3 parts. Stolen & replaced portion = 2 / 3.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must water be mixed with milk to gain 16 2/3% by selling the mixture at cost price?
questions.explanation: Gain% = 16 2/3 % = 50/3 % = 1/6. Ratio of water to milk = 1 : 6.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 50 litres of milk. 10 litres is taken out and replaced by water. 10 litres is again taken out and replaced by water. How much milk is left in the vessel?
Gold is 19 times as heavy as water and copper is 9 times as heavy as water. In what ratio should these be mixed to get an alloy 15 times as heavy as water?
A mixture of 150 litres of wine and water contains 20% water. How much more water should be added so that water becomes 25% of the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Wine = 80% of 150 = 120 L. In new mixture, wine is 75%. Total new mixture = 120 / 0.75 = 160 L. Water added = 160 - 150 = 10 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must tea at Rs. 240/kg be mixed with tea at Rs. 280/kg so that the mixture is worth Rs. 260/kg?

Three glasses of equal volume contain mixture of milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1, 3 : 1, and 3 : 2. If all three are poured into a single vessel, find the ratio of milk to water in the final mixture.
questions.explanation: Volumes: 3, 4, 5. LCM = 60. Glass 1 (scale 20): Milk = 40, Water = 20. Glass 2 (scale 15): Milk = 45, Water = 15. Glass 3 (scale 12): Milk = 36, Water = 24. Total Milk = 40 + 45 + 36 = 121. Total Water = 20 + 15 + 24 = 59. Ratio = 121 : 59.

questions.questionText: A trader has 50 kg of pulses, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. What is the quantity sold at 18% profit?
A vessel contains 60 litres of pure acid. 10 litres is taken out and replaced by water. Then 10 litres of the mixture is taken out and replaced by water. What is the amount of pure acid left?
A 45-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.explanation: Initial: Milk = 36 L, Water = 9 L. For ratio 3 : 2 with 36 L milk: 3 parts = 36 => 1 part = 12 L. Water needed = 2 * 12 = 24 L. Water to add = 24 - 9 = 15 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio should two qualities of coffee powder costing Rs. 180 and Rs. 260 per kg be mixed to obtain a blend worth Rs. 210 per kg?
A milkman has 20 litres of milk. He mixes 5 litres of water. What is the percentage of milk in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Total volume = 25 L. Milk = 20 L. Percentage = (20 / 25) * 100% = 80%.

questions.questionText: Two vessels contain milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2 and 7 : 3. In what ratio should the contents of the two vessels be mixed to get a mixture containing milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1?
From a cask of 63 litres of wine, 9 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. If this is done twice in total, how much wine remains in the cask?
questions.explanation: After each replacement, the fraction of wine retained is 1 - 9/63 = 6/7. After two rounds, the wine remaining is 63*(6/7)^2 = 324/7 litres, or about 46.29 litres.

questions.questionText: A 35-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. If 7 litres of water is added, what will be the new ratio of milk to water?
questions.explanation: Initial: Milk = 28 L, Water = 7 L. Adding 7 L water: New Water = 14 L. New ratio = 28 : 14 = 2 : 1.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must grocer mix two varieties of tea worth Rs. 60/kg and Rs. 65/kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 68.20/kg he gains 10%?
A container has 50 litres of juice. 5 litres is drawn out and replaced with water. This process is repeated 3 times. What is the percentage of juice left?

Two vessels A and B contain spirits and water in the ratio 5 : 2 and 7 : 6 respectively. Find the ratio in which these mixtures be mixed to obtain a new mixture in vessel C containing spirit and water in the ratio 8 : 5?
How much water should be added to 300 ml of 20% acid solution to make it a 15% acid solution?
questions.explanation: Acid = 20% of 300 = 60 ml. In 15% solution, total volume = 60 / 0.15 = 400 ml. Water to add = 400 - 300 = 100 ml.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains a mixture of 1 part water and 3 parts syrup. How much of the mixture must be drawn off and replaced with water so that the mixture may be half water and half syrup?
questions.explanation: Syrup initially = 3/4. Target syrup = 1/2. Let fraction removed and replaced with water (0% syrup) be x. (3/4)(1 - x) = 1/2 => 1 - x = (1/2)*(4/3) = 2/3 => x = 1/3.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must an alloy containing 80% copper be mixed with an alloy containing 90% copper to obtain an alloy containing 84% copper?
In what ratio must water be mixed with milk to gain 20% by selling the mixture at cost price?
questions.concept: Direct Water Ratio on CP Sale

questions.questionText: A merchant has 120 kg of wheat, part of which he sells at 10% gain and the rest at 25% gain. Overall he gains 15%. How much wheat was sold at 25% gain?
A jar contains 60 litres of milk. 12 litres of milk is taken out and replaced by water. If this process is repeated twice more (total 3 times), find the quantity of milk remaining.

Two vessels A and B contain mixtures of milk and water in the ratio 4 : 5 and 5 : 1 respectively. In what ratio should quantities be taken from A and B to form a mixture in which milk and water are in the ratio 5 : 4?
questions.explanation: Milk in A = 4/9 = 8/18. Milk in B = 5/6 = 15/18. Target milk in mixture = 5/9 = 10/18. By Alligation: (15/18 - 10/18) : (10/18 - 8/18) = 5 : 2.

questions.questionText: How many kg of salt at 42 paise per kg must a man mix with 25 kg of salt at 24 paise per kg so that he may gain 25% by selling the mixture at 40 paise per kg?
questions.explanation: Mean CP = 40 / 1.25 = 32 paise/kg. By Alligation: (32 - 24) : (42 - 32) = 8 : 10 = 4 : 5. 5 parts = 25 kg => 1 part = 5 kg. 4 parts = 4 * 5 = 20 kg.

questions.questionText: A 40-litre mixture of milk and water contains 10% water. How many litres of water must be added to make water 20% in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk = 90% of 40 = 36 L. In new mixture: 80% = 36 L => Total = 45 L. Water to add = 45 - 40 = 5 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a merchant mix two varieties of oil costing Rs. 70/litre and Rs. 90/litre to obtain a mixture worth Rs. 78/litre?

A cask contains 100 litres of wine. 10 litres of wine is drawn and replaced by water. 10 litres of mixture is drawn again and replaced by water. Find the ratio of wine to water in the resulting mixture.
A mixture of 125 gallons of wine and water contains 20% wine. How much wine must be added to make it 25% of the total mixture?
questions.explanation: Water = 80% of 125 = 100 gallons. In new mixture, water is 75%. New total = 100 / 0.75 = 133.33 gallons. Wine to add = 133.33 - 125 = 8.33 gallons (8 1/3 gal).

questions.questionText: Two vessels A and B contain mixtures of spirit and water in the ratio 5 : 3 and 2 : 3 respectively. Find the ratio in which these are to be mixed to get a mixture containing half spirit and half water.
A grocer mixes 26 kg of tea at Rs. 20/kg with 30 kg of tea at Rs. 36/kg and sells the mixture at Rs. 30/kg. What is his profit percentage?
A bottle contains 30 litres of milk. 3 litres is taken out and replaced by water. The process is repeated 3 times. What is the quantity of milk in the final mixture?
In what ratio must an 80% acid solution be mixed with a 50% acid solution to produce a 60% acid solution?
A merchant blends two varieties of tea, one costing Rs. 180/kg and another Rs. 200/kg in the ratio 5 : 3. If he sells the blend at Rs. 210/kg, what is his profit percentage?
A mixture contains alcohol and water in the ratio 4 : 3. If 5 litres of water is added to the mixture, the ratio becomes 4 : 5. Find the quantity of alcohol in the given mixture.
From a container of 50 litres of milk, 5 litres is replaced with water. This process is repeated 2 times in total. What is the ratio of milk to water now?
How many litres of water must be added to 16 litres of a 25% salt solution to make it a 20% solution?
questions.explanation: Salt = 25% of 16 = 4 litres. In 20% solution, total volume = 4 / 0.20 = 20 litres. Water to add = 20 - 16 = 4 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must milk and water be mixed so that on selling at cost price, there is a profit of 25%?
Two alloys of gold and copper contain gold in the ratio 7 : 2 and 7 : 11. If equal weights are melted to form a third alloy C, find the ratio of gold to copper in C.
questions.explanation: Alloy 1 (ratio 7:2, scale by 2): Gold = 14/18, Copper = 4/18. Alloy 2 (ratio 7:11): Gold = 7/18, Copper = 11/18. Total Gold = 14 + 7 = 21. Total Copper = 4 + 11 = 15. Ratio = 21 : 15 = 7 : 5.

questions.questionText: A jar full of whisky contains 40% alcohol. A part of this whisky is replaced by another containing 19% alcohol and now the percentage of alcohol was found to be 26%. What fraction of the whisky was replaced?
